result.target_topic: Asset Retirement and Lease Amortization Policy
result.target_summary: Upon retirement or disposition, related costs and accumulated depreciation are removed with any gain or loss recorded; finance lease assets and leasehold improvements are amortized over the shorter of the lease term or useful life.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures state that property and equipment are stated at cost (less accumulated depreciation in 2024) and depreciated using the straight-line method based on estimated useful lives (3-5 years in 2023, 3-7 years in 2024). D040 cites P045_S001 and P045_S002; D050 cites P052_S001 and P052_S002.

Both disclosures cover the derecognition of assets upon retirement/disposition (removing cost and accumulated depreciation, recording gain/loss) and the amortization of finance lease assets and leasehold improvements. D040 cites P045_S003, P045_S005, and P045_S006; D051 cites P052_S003, P052_S005, and P052_S006.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting Policy for Property and Equipment
comparisons.peer_summary: Property and equipment are stated at cost, with depreciation and amortization calculated on a straight-line basis over estimated useful lives of 2 to 15 years for equipment, 34 to 44 years for buildings, and based on the shorter of lease terms or useful lives for leasehold improvements.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose their accounting policy for the amortization of leasehold improvements and finance lease assets. NVDA states that these assets are amortized over the shorter of the expected lease term or the estimated useful life of the asset. Similarly, AMD's policy for leasehold improvements is measured by the shorter of the remaining terms of the leases or the estimated useful economic lives of the improvements. However, AMD provides specific useful life ranges for equipment (2-15 years) and buildings (34-44 years), whereas NVDA's text does not specify the numerical useful lives for these categories.

sentences.text: Leasehold improvements and assets recorded under finance leases are amortized over the shorter of the expected lease term or the estimated useful life of the asset.

Depreciation and amortization are provided on a straight-line basis over the estimated useful lives of two to 15 years for equipment, 34 to 44 years for buildings, and leasehold improvements are measured by the shorter of the remaining terms of the leases or the estimated useful economic lives of the improvements.
